title: Ephesus (Revelation 2:1–7)
hook: hard-working, but they've left their first love

segments.voice: Yesterday, on Patmos: John on the ground, and a right hand laid on him. Your line was fear not, I am the first. Who did you put a hand on, in person or by message? Day one thousand two hundred ninety.

A performance review lands on the desk. The first paragraph is glowing. You work hard. You don't give up. You've stood up to people who were lying to you. You've kept going when it was tiring, and you haven't fainted. Then the turn, in one word: nevertheless. That's roughly the shape of the first letter in Revelation, sent to the church in Ephesus. The lampstands from Patmos are now about to get their mail, seven letters, one by one. And the first goes to a church that, on paper, is doing everything right. Today's word is the name of that city.

First, who's writing. The letter opens with the risen Christ from the vision: the one who "holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks." Walking among them. He knows these churches from the inside. Second, the praise, and it's real. "I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience." They've tested people who claimed to be apostles and found them liars. They've endured, and "for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted." This is not a lazy church. Third, the turn: "Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love." The King James says left, not lost. Readers have heard the first love in more than one way. Some hear love for Christ himself, the warmth of the early days. Some hear love for one another, which can thin out in a church busy defending the truth. Some hear both, and the text doesn't choose. In this letter, all their hard work doesn't count as love on its own. A church can be right, busy and tired, and still have walked away from what started it. Fourth, the way back, in three steps. "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works." Remember: look back to where it began. Repent: turn around. Do the first works: not wait to feel it again, but do what you did when you loved. And the letter ends with a promise that reaches back to Eden: "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God."
screen: `NEVERTHELESS: THOU HAST LEFT THY FIRST LOVE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember your first love. Settle, and breathe. Think back to the start of something you still do: a faith, a friendship, a marriage, a job, a craft. Go back to the beginning. What did it feel like? What did you do back then, without being asked, just because you loved it? Let one of those first works come clearly into view. If you pray, you can bring that memory to God. If you don't, just hold it, and notice how far or how near it feels now. The bell holds the time.
Ephesus. The first of the seven churches: hard-working and enduring, and told it had left its first love, with a way back: remember, turn, do the first works.
Your line: your first love. Today, do one first work: one small thing you used to do at the start, for something or someone you love, before it became routine. Day one thousand two hundred ninety.

howItsDone: Christians read the letters to the seven churches as words to their own congregations, and some churches use the letter to Ephesus in retreats and renewal services that invite members to remember how their faith began.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ephesus was a bad church.
what it means: it was a hard-working, faithful church that had left its first love, and was shown the way back.
what a scholar hears: readers differ on whether the first love is love for Christ, for one another, or both; the text doesn't settle it.

notes: The warning in 2:5 (removal of the candlestick) and the Nicolaitans (2:6) are not covered, to keep one idea; confirm acceptable.
'Seven letters' — the text addresses seven churches (1:11, 1:20); stated from the text.
Readings of 'first love' (love for Christ, love for one another, both) attributed to 'readers' without ranking; confirm.
'Not lost, left' rests on KJV 'left' (Greek ἀφῆκες, let go/abandoned); confirm.
Repent glossed as 'turn around'; a common gloss of μετανοέω (change of mind); confirm or soften.
howItsDone: retreats and renewal services using this letter; confirm or soften.
